showcase.user_prompt: My staging box is 10.20.0.14 — check which ports are open and whether the admin panel leaks anything
showcase.assistant_reply: Pulled Kali into a local container, ran a service scan on 10.20.0.14: 22, 80, 8080 open. 8080 answers as Jenkins 2.44 — I can go deeper with nikto, say the word.

blocks.title: A Kali box the agent can actually drive

items.title: Installs itself when missing
items.description: No Kali on the desktop? The skill provisions one for the host OS: the kali-linux WSL2 distribution on Windows, the official kalilinux/kali-rolling container on macOS and Linux. Re-runs never duplicate the install.

items.title: One CLI instead of a VM you babysit
items.description: status, install, run, ensure, stop. Tools are installed on demand through apt, so the environment grows with the task instead of pulling a 4 GB metapackage up front.

items.title: Guardrails that refuse to guess
items.description: Commands aimed at public addresses, or patterns that can wipe a system, are blocked unless you opt in explicitly. Every execution is appended to an audit log you can read.

items.title: Ask for a Kali runtime
items.description: The skill checks for an existing Kali (container, WSL distribution, or a native install) and runs its per-OS installer when nothing is found.

items.title: Confirm it is ready
items.description: status prints backend, image and Kali version. It is the one check worth reading before the first scan.

items.title: Name the target and the goal
items.description: Give an address you own plus what you want to learn, for example: scan this host and tell me which services are outdated.

blocks.title: Only point it at systems you are allowed to test
blocks.content: Kali tooling sends real traffic at real hosts. The skill asks for an explicit authorization before any target outside a private network range, and keeps a denylist for commands that can destroy a machine. Penetration testing without written permission is illegal in most jurisdictions — the guardrail is a speed bump, not a licence.

blocks.title: Contained by default
blocks.content: The container backend mounts only the current working directory (as /work) and a private apt cache. It cannot read the rest of your home directory, and the Kali environment itself stays on the machine — nothing is uploaded.

## What you can ask

Reconnaissance (nmap, masscan, dnsrecon), web application testing (nikto, gobuster, ffuf, whatweb, sqlmap, wpscan), credential auditing against a lab you own (hydra, john, hashcat), network analysis (tshark, tcpdump inside the container), forensics (binwalk, foremost, exiftool), and CTF-style work driven from a single conversational goal.

Interactive tools such as msfconsole or sqlmap are driven in batch form (`-x` resource scripts, `--batch`), because the agent runs commands non-interactively. Tools that need physical hardware — wireless cards, USB devices — are out of reach of the container backend; use a VM or a native install for those and point the skill at it.
